code_first.q: On a mini-whiteboard, complete the missing assignment so the code prints MAT-27. Use uppercase conversion and concatenation; then test.
code_first.code:
student = "Matilda"
group = "27"
first = student.left(3)
code = ____________________
print(code)
p: Identify the first three characters of Matilda.
Use .upper and join the hyphen and group as strings.
Check that the exact output is MAT-27.
code_first.a:
MODEL OCR ERL
student = "Matilda"
group = "27"
first = student.left(3)
code = first.upper + "-" + group
print(code)

EXPECTED OUTPUT
MAT-27

original_exam_questions:
Trace the following OCR Exam Reference Language. Write the exact TWO lines printed. Show how the substring is selected. [4 marks]

username = "TylerFox"
prefix = username.left(2)
suffix = username.substring(5, 3)
code = prefix.upper + "-" + suffix.lower
print(code)
print(code.length)

prefix = "Ty"; suffix = "Fox" (begin at index 5 and take 3 characters).
First output: TY-fox.
Second output: 6 (two letters, hyphen, three letters).
Marking: correct parts (1), correct case and concatenation (1), exact first output (1), correct length (1).

A school generates a pupil identifier from the FIRST three letters of firstName and the LAST three letters of surname, both uppercase, separated by a hyphen.

With firstName = "Georgia" and surname = "Mitchell", the required output is GEO-ELL.

Write an OCR Exam Reference Language algorithm that prints "Invalid" if EITHER name has fewer than three characters; otherwise print the identifier. [6 marks]

MODEL OCR ERL
firstName = "Georgia"
surname = "Mitchell"
if firstName.length >= 3 AND surname.length >= 3 then
    firstPart = firstName.left(3)
    lastPart = surname.right(3)
    print(firstPart.upper + "-" + lastPart.upper)
else
    print("Invalid")
endif

Expected output: GEO-ELL.
Marking: checks lengths of both inputs (2), correct left(3) (1), correct right(3) (1), uppercase and hyphen concatenation (1), correct valid/invalid output paths (1). Accept equivalent correct OCR ERL.

A programmer intends the following program to print MAT-27, but it produces the wrong result.

student = "Matilda"
group = "27"
code = student.substring(1, 3) + group
print(code)

(a) State the output of the original program. [1]
(b) Identify THREE changes needed to produce MAT-27. [3]
(c) Rewrite the string-handling statements using OCR Exam Reference Language so the program prints MAT-27. [2]
[6 marks total]

(a) ati27.
(b) Select characters starting at index 0, not index 1; convert the letters to uppercase; insert a quoted hyphen between the letters and group.
(c) One acceptable answer:
first = student.left(3)
code = first.upper + "-" + group
print(code)
Alternative: student.substring(0, 3) instead of left(3).
Marking: exact original output (1), three distinct corrections (3), valid slicing and uppercase (1), correct concatenation and print (1).

optional_original_challenge.coreHint: Use OCR ERL .left, .right and .substring(start, count); a quoted hyphen is a single string character.

stretch.task: Adapt the worked example for student = "Harrison" and club = "Robotics": produce SON:ROB using right(3), left(3), .upper and a colon. Then print the length. Write OCR ERL.
stretch.hint: The last three letters of Harrison are son; the first three of Robotics are Rob. A colon counts as one character.
stretch.answer:
MODEL OCR ERL
student = "Harrison"
club = "Robotics"
a = student.right(3)
b = club.left(3)
code = a.upper + ":" + b.upper
print(code)
print(code.length)

Outputs: SON:ROB and 7.

mastery.task: Design an OCR ERL algorithm that accepts a surname and a two-character year code. If surname has fewer than three characters OR year code is not exactly two characters, print Invalid. Otherwise print the first three surname letters in uppercase, followed by a hyphen and the year code. Give one normal, one boundary and one invalid test.
mastery.hint: Check both lengths before calling .left(3). Use .length for each condition and concatenate strings with +.
mastery.answer:
MODEL OCR ERL
surname = input("Surname")
yearCode = input("Two-character year code")
if surname.length >= 3 AND yearCode.length == 2 then
    prefix = surname.left(3)
    print(prefix.upper + "-" + yearCode)
else
    print("Invalid")
endif

Tests: surname = "Mason", yearCode = "27" -> MAS-27 (normal); surname = "Lee", yearCode = "27" -> LEE-27 (boundary valid); surname = "Li", yearCode = "27" -> Invalid (invalid). Also test a one-character year code.
